p-ud-1.q: The speed of light $c$, gravitational constant $G$, and Planck's constant $h$ are taken as fundamental units. Find the dimension of time in this system.
A physical quantity $X$ is expressed as $X = \varepsilon_0 L \frac{\Delta V}{\Delta t}$. Find the matching dimensional formula for $X$.
If momentum $P$, area $A$, and time $T$ are taken as fundamental quantities, find the dimensional formula for energy.

p-kin-1.q: A particle moves along a straight line such that its velocity varies with position as $v = 4\sqrt{x}$ (where $x$ is in meters). Compute the acceleration of the particle in $\text{m/s}^2$.

A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate $\alpha = 2 \text{ m/s}^2$ for some time, then decelerates at $\beta = 4 \text{ m/s}^2$ to come to rest. If total time elapsed is 6 seconds, find the maximum velocity reached.
The displacement of a body moving along a straight line matches $x = 2t^3 - 6t^2 + 12$. Find the velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero.

p-nlm-1.q: A block of mass 10 kg is placed on a smooth wedge of inclination 30°. The whole wedge is accelerated horizontally so that the block remains stationary relative to the wedge. Find the horizontal acceleration in $\text{m/s}^2$. (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)

Three blocks of masses 2 kg, 3 kg, and 5 kg are connected by light strings and pulled horizontally along a frictionless surface by a force of 20 N. Find the tension in the string between the 3 kg and 5 kg blocks.
A mass of 5 kg is suspended by two light strings making angles of 45° and 45° with the horizontal ceiling. Calculate the tension in each string. (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
